title: RCC Bridge Line: Declaration, Mutual Aid and Coast Guard Helicopter, 12:15

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EOC Command Desk, RCC Bridge

caller.name: RCC Duty Officer
caller.label: Oregon OEM Regional Coordination Center, Salem

callee.name: EOC Command Desk
callee.label: MCEM Director, Marlow County EOC, Kellerton

transcript.speaker: EOC Command
transcript.text: Marlow County EOC, Command.

transcript.speaker: RCC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Marlow County, this is the Oregon OEM Regional Coordination Center duty officer on the bridge line. You're breaking up a little, so I'll keep it short. First item: we need your signed local emergency declaration before we can take a request for a state declaration to the Governor's office. Do you have one signed?

transcript.speaker: RCC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Second item. Who is your incident commander right now? And who signs for the county if your Director isn't reachable? I need a name for the log, not just a title.

transcript.speaker: RCC Duty Officer
transcript.text: So you know where you stand: every coastal county from Clatsop to Curry is calling in. State teams will not reach you by road for at least 72 hours. Plan on that.

transcript.speaker: RCC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Tillamook County Emergency Management emailed your EOC inbox at 12:12. Their own waterfront is flooded. Once a route opens they can offer a six-person CERT team and one ambulance, but they cannot cross the Neskin grade. They'll need a written request from you that says where those people should go.

transcript.speaker: RCC Duty Officer
transcript.text: I have the Coast Guard command center on the bridge. Patching them in now.

transcript.speaker: Coast Guard
transcript.text: Marlow County, Coast Guard command center. We have one helicopter tasked to the whole Oregon coast. Send us your priorities through the RCC, in order. We cannot commit before fourteen hundred.

transcript.speaker: Coast Guard
transcript.text: For each priority we need the number of patients, their condition, the location, a landing zone, and any hazards like wires, debris or crowds. Then we can sequence you against the other counties.

transcript.speaker: RCC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Marlow, I'm keeping the bridge open. Scan the signed declaration and your mutual aid and air requests to the RCC inbox as soon as you can. What time should I expect them?

transcript.speaker: EOC Command
transcript.text: Stand by, RCC.

voiceStyles.RCC Duty Officer: Woman in her 40s, calm and clipped, working several lines at once, phones ringing in a busy coordination room behind her
voiceStyles.Coast Guard: Man in his 30s, military radio cadence, even and brief, slightly tinny over the patched line
voiceStyles.EOC Command: Tired EOC staffer, generator hum in the room

instructorNote: This call is about getting outside help: the Director should sign the local emergency declaration and send it to OEM through the RCC with a request for a state declaration, name MCEM EOC Command as the lead with the Sheriff and the Fire District under it, and say who signs as alternate. Watch whether Command sends ranked mutual aid requests to Tillamook and Lincoln counties and gives the Coast Guard air priorities (oxygen and medical transport for the Station 3 apron first), and whether it plans on 72 hours with no help by road.
